claude.sample_unit: consultation sessions rated (1000 pre- and 1000 post-optimization)

links.outcome: Response quality before vs after expert-review-guided corrective optimization
links.effect: Good overall quality rose from 652 (65.2%) to 743 (74.3%); clinically appropriate rose from 614 (61.4%) to 874 (87.4%), both P<.001.
links.quote: After expert-guided optimization, the number of sessions rated good (n=1000) in overall quality (the response fully resolving the caregiver's question with actionable information) increased from 652 (65.2%) to 743 (74.3%), and the number rated clinically appropriate increased from 614 (61.4%) to 874 (87.4%, both P<.001).

links.outcome: Turn-level deficiency rate in deployed LLM responses
links.effect: Deficiency rate declined from 19.4% (790/4073 turns) to 6.9% (236/3419 turns; OR 0.30) but persisted, mainly suboptimal clinical recommendations.
links.quote: The turn-level deficiency rate declined from 19.4% (790/4073 turns) to 6.9% (236/3419 turns; odds ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.24-0.37; P<.001), with suboptimal clinical recommendations (not optimally tailored to the child's age or clinical context) remaining the most frequent category.

openai.sample_unit: consultation sessions (2000 underwent expert response-quality evaluation)

links.outcome: Expert-rated overall response quality and clinical appropriateness
links.effect: After bundled expert-guided optimization, good overall quality increased from 652 (65.2%) to 743 (74.3%), and clinical appropriateness increased from 614 (61.4%) to 874 (87.4%, both P<.001); 1000 sessions per round.
links.quote: After expert-guided optimization, the number of sessions rated good (n=1000) in overall quality (the response fully resolving the caregiver's question with actionable information) increased from 652 (65.2%) to 743 (74.3%), and the number rated clinically appropriate increased from 614 (61.4%) to 874 (87.4%, both P<.001).

links.outcome: Expert-assessed response deficiencies, including suboptimal clinical recommendations
links.effect: Deficiencies persisted after optimization: 6.9% (236/3419 turns), versus 19.4% (790/4073 turns) before optimization; odds ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.24-0.37; P<.001. Suboptimal clinical recommendations remained the most frequent category.
links.quote: The turn-level deficiency rate declined from 19.4% (790/4073 turns) to 6.9% (236/3419 turns; odds ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.24-0.37; P<.001), with suboptimal clinical recommendations (not optimally tailored to the child's age or clinical context) remaining the most frequent category.

screen.practice: expert-guided optimization including prompt revision, knowledge-base expansion, and validation rules
screen.reason: The study evaluates a live, deployed pediatric LLM assistant used by real caregivers and compares response quality before versus after expert-guided iterative optimization (prompt revision, knowledge base/tool expansion, and validation rules).
